Subject: Access & Admin Audit Streams — retention windows, export formats, and deletion proof

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for taking this. Our compliance team at Acme Health is finalizing the SOC2 evidence set and we need clarity on two streams: access logs (auth, token events, API gateway logs) and admin audit logs (role changes, config changes, RBAC events). Specifically: 

- What are the default retention windows for each stream in the hosted product? Are there documented options for extending retention?
- What export formats do you support for bulk exports (CSV/NDJSON/Parquet)? Do exports include checksums or manifests suitable for chain-of-custody?
- If a customer requests deletion of logs tied to a subject (legal request), what does the deletion workflow look like and can you provide an auditable proof of deletion?

We attached an initial spreadsheet with the items we want in the export (initial_log_requirements.xlsx). High level answers are fine for now; the auditors will follow up with specifics.

Would appreciate a response by Thursday so we can slot this into our audit window.

—Jake
Security Ops, Acme Health

Hi Jake —

Thanks — answered inline at a high level below. Attaching a machine-friendly spec for exports (access_logs_export_spec.csv) and a short summary you can share with auditors.

Summary answers:
- Retention defaults: access logs (API/auth events, request metadata) = 90 days; admin audit logs (RBAC changes, config edits) = 365 days. These defaults are for Hosted API customers on standard plans.
- Extended retention: Yes — Dedicated and Private customers can opt into longer retention (1, 3, 7 years) via Reserved or Enterprise packages. For Hosted customers we provide a managed long-term export option (monthly snapshots to S3-compatible storage) as an add-on.
- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), compressed CSV (gzip), and Apache Parquet for analytics pipelines. Each bulk export bundle includes a manifest.json with SHA256 checksums for each file and a signed export token (HMAC) to allow verification of integrity and issuer.
- Export SLA: Typically available as a self-service bulk export within 7 days; for playbook exports (for audits) we offer a 30-day SLA and can push to your signed S3 bucket or provide a secure one-time download link.
- Deletion workflow and proof: We perform a two-step deletion for hosted data: soft-delete (marked, retained for 30 days for recovery and legal holds) followed by irreversible purge. For each purge we generate a deletion manifest that lists file identifiers, timestamps, and SHA256 of the final storage objects prior to purge. If requested, we sign that manifest and include the chain-of-custody (who requested, approver, job-id). That signed manifest is considered our proof of deletion for audit purposes.

Notes / caveats:
- If logs have been exported and stored outside Redwood (your side), Redwood cannot revoke or delete those external copies — we document that in the export contract.
- For Private deployments we provide on-prem playbooks and possible air-gapped transfer procedures.
- Cross-region residency: exports will be generated from the region the tenant is pinned to; we can produce region-specific export artifacts on request.

Action items:
- Confirm whether Acme needs the signed deletion manifests included in the SOC2 artifact bundle; if yes, we can produce a template and a sample for your auditors.
- If you want the monthly S3 snapshot add-on, Monica on my team can spin up the export config and share costs.

Attaching: access_logs_export_spec.csv (fields + example rows).

Thanks,

Hi Jake —

Short answers to your three asks, and next steps: 

1) Manifest & signed token: yes — bulk export bundles generated by Redwood include the manifest.json and the signed export token by default. We will mark that as a mandatory inclusion in the audit bundle.

2) Purge artifact contents: for hosted purges we can include storage object identifiers (object key / path in the S3 bucket we manage), timestamps, and SHA256 values in the signed deletion manifest. We cannot, for security reasons, include low-level ephemeral host identifiers, but the object keys and checksums are sufficient for reconciliation with our storage ledger.

3) Encryption: exports in transit use TLS1.3; at-rest encryption is AES-256 by default for managed S3 snapshots and our internal object store. For customer-managed buckets we accept server-side encrypted uploads (SSE-S3 / SSE-KMS) or client-side envelopes as requested.

Chain-of-custody and additional evidence: we offer a one-page playbook that documents the export generation, package verification, and purge signing steps. If you want, we can produce a sample signed deletion manifest for a redacted dataset so your auditors have a template to review.

Next steps:
- I will share the audit playbook link and a redacted sample manifest.
- If Acme wants the monthly snapshot add-on, Monica will send pricing and a PO template; otherwise we can run a one-off export for this audit window.
